title.narrative: Building a culture of resilience in Africa and Small Islands Developing States (SIDS) through innovation

description.narrative: The overarching objective of this project is for UNESCO to foster a culture of resilience in Africa and Small Island Developing States (SIDS), through innovative approaches. Aligned to the priorities of the pilot countries - Ethiopia, Djibouti, Rwanda, the Pacific SIDS, Solomon Islands, Tuvalu, Kiribati and Fiji, the project addresses climate change adaptation and disaster risk reduction. Two outcomes are targeted, firstly, by reducing economic losses from hazards by comprehensively mapping supply chains and conducting risk assessments of major industries. Secondly, the project seeks to strengthen disaster preparedness and response through consolidated data sources, improved data sharing and visualisation techniques. The project also emphasizes the enhancement of capacities to ensure resilience of industries and the protection of livelihoods. The project aims to build community resilience through innovative practices, technological know-how and capacity building initiatives. This approach is critical for preservation of heritage as well as sustainable growth of tourism, maintenance of sustainable livelihoods and resilience of populations at large.
